Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software that lets a merchant sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and lets the buyer receive the complete result in its existing application.

We request $38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from award acceptance. The outcome is two independently operated merchant services, each used by an independent buyer, and two independent buyer operators. T2 operates the same useful service through two independently operated testnet facilitators; T3 establishes both merchant installations on mainnet under their reviewed production configurations. The work progresses from installed services by day 30 to recurring testnet use by day 90 and maintainable mainnet operation by day 150.

A purchase connects four records: the buyer’s approved request, the settled transfer, the complete usable output and the merchant’s fulfillment or accounting. The application keeps that connection through interrupted delivery, a changed source edition and transfer to another maintainer.

The existing product is the starting point. The award funds reusable Stellar integration, source and receiving adaptations, deployment, monitoring and recovery improvements required by the selected independent services. Those improvements return to the public product.

Customer problem, need and adoption

Our first customer is a recurring API/data-service operator or the agency implementing that service in its customer’s application. We commission a complete recurring task: an authorized source or query, its selected population and period, the useful report, file or application result, and the engineer who will maintain the service. The commissioning payer buys that installation and handover; the independent buyer pays for its useful resource. These roles can belong to different organizations.

For an analyst, completion means the entire selected population with its original units, time basis and usable report. For an agent application, it means the approved result within its aggregate task budget. A task spanning paid pages remains open until every agreed page is received. A prepaid call retains the selected pass and its consumed allowance when defaults change. The merchant connects those completed results to its offer, fulfillment and accounting. This makes a purchase usable in the customer’s continuing work.

A public Base implementation report describes two settled USDC payments while the resource remained absent from Bazaar discovery after twenty-four hours. A separate operator later reported successful indexing after new settlements and described the facilitator’s extension-response diagnostics. These first-party accounts distinguish payment, discovery and usable service delivery, supplying cross-ecosystem implementation learning for our Stellar integration. Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar supplies native payment authorization and settlement for the customer’s reviewed operation. In the x402 Exact Stellar flow, the buyer signs a Soroban authorization entry for a token transfer with its payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. The facilitator submits the authorization under the selected network and fee policy. Sponsored settlement lets the buyer pay in the selected supported token while the facilitator covers the transaction fee. Existing Stellar wallets, token contracts and payment services provide this native foundation.

The merchant and buyer workspaces retain the HTTP endpoint and method or MCP tool and arguments, request-body identity, selected source or query, and accepted payment option. Their approval and signer integration check the original operation before dispatch. The retained purchase then connects the native transfer to its complete received output and required fulfillment. Buyers keep wallet and aggregate spending authority; merchants keep control of resources, terms and order actions. The grant applies these native-payment and application responsibilities to the selected customers’ actual installations.

The ledger records the transfer; the private workspaces retain the source selection, request, complete output and fulfillment history. The original transaction identity connects these records so an interrupted delivery can continue from its settled purchase. The maintained native signer and facilitator compose the existing x402 packages and token contracts. The facilitator already accepts explicit testnet or pubnet configuration, allowed assets and recipients, fee ceilings, distinct signing accounts and admission/drain controls. The funded deployment supplies the selected operators’ actual network, RPC, fee policy and operating configuration. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery model. Defined architecture and operating behavior

The architecture has six components: a private merchant source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the Stellar SDK and facilitator; private buyer approval and spending state; retained delivery records and complete output; and merchant fulfillment/accounting.

Select and publish. The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.

Connect the source. Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.

Approve and pay. The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.

Settle and receive. The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.

Use and account. The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.

Recover and hand over. Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. New contracts are outside this six-package request; the product uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

Threat response and outcome measurement

The T2 threat model and monitoring plan are included in the 50-hour/$4,750 response package. Each installation records its source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network, facilitator, protected records, observation sources, reviewed thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders.

It covers changed offers or approvals, incorrect payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted delivery, lost observation and restoration of the wrong generation. The customer operates an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Both retain notification and acknowledgment, financial and delivery states, response/recovery times, corrections and the receiving engineer’s reopening after restart. Monitoring gaps remain visible until observation resumes.

Delivery capacity, payment timing and sustainability

Bryce is accountable for allocating contributors and operating resources to the six packages. The retained resource study uses 400 hours over 150 days. Its lowest examined timely allocation is 25 engineering hours plus eight integration/handover hours per week. This is a modeled allocation; named contributor availability and payment arrangements are being finalized against the actual award date.

SCF’s four payments would be $3,800 at award acceptance, then $7,600, $11,400 and $15,200 after the respective deliverables are approved. These payment amounts differ from tranche delivery costs. The USD-equivalent award is paid in XLM; the XLM quantity uses CF XLMUSD_RR, or SDF’s selected qualifying alternative, reported on the actual award payment day, under the Official Rules.

Grant and accepted commercial work share one contributor capacity plan. A commissioned workshare adds its actual hours, dependencies and acceptance dates; available hours are allocated once. Bryce reconciles the combined schedule and expected collections before agreeing dated work, using separately named capacity or agreed timing changes. The maintained Grant Operations workspace keeps supplier work and invoices, reviewed statement cash movements and dated installation capacity in the same retained grant case, with complete source-linked reports and customer receiving.

The resource model makes the working-capital requirement explicit. With its labor-accrual assumptions, additional peak cash is $17,250 at a 14-day review/payment lag, $23,275 at 30 days and $26,600 at 60 days. Opening cash and a committed bridge or contributor deferral have not been entered. Actual available funds, client collections and agreed contributor payment timing must cover the modeled requirement before the corresponding delivery commitments are made.

Each tranche completion form is due within 90 calendar days of the preceding payment. For an anticipated delay, we will obtain SDF’s written acknowledgment before the original deadline and use a revised deadline only when confirmed in writing.

Sustainability comes from reusable open-source deployment and receiving capabilities, paid customer-specific implementation and separately scoped care. Workorders retain delivery effort, included corrections, support responsibilities, acceptance and collections. Reusable work completed before award is removed from the remaining estimate, keeping the grant focused on the agreed prospective Stellar development.

## Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software that lets a merchant sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and lets the buyer receive the complete result in its existing application.

We request **$38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from award acceptance**. The outcome is two independently operated merchant services, each used by an independent buyer, and two independent buyer operators. T2 operates the same useful service through **two independently operated testnet facilitators**; T3 establishes **both merchant installations on mainnet** under their reviewed production configurations. The work progresses from installed services by day 30 to recurring testnet use by day 90 and maintainable mainnet operation by day 150.

A purchase connects four records: the buyer’s approved request, the settled transfer, the complete usable output and the merchant’s fulfillment or accounting. The application keeps that connection through interrupted delivery, a changed source edition and transfer to another maintainer.

The existing product is the starting point. The award funds reusable Stellar integration, source and receiving adaptations, deployment, monitoring and recovery improvements required by the selected independent services. Those improvements return to the public product.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The architecture has six components: a private merchant source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the Stellar SDK and facilitator; private buyer approval and spending state; retained delivery records and complete output; and merchant fulfillment/accounting.

**Select and publish.** The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.

**Connect the source.** Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.

**Approve and pay.** The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.

**Settle and receive.** The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.

**Use and account.** The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.

**Recover and hand over.** Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. New contracts are outside this six-package request; the product uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

## Threat response and outcome measurement

The T2 threat model and monitoring plan are included in the 50-hour/$4,750 response package. Each installation records its source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network, facilitator, protected records, observation sources, reviewed thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders.

It covers changed offers or approvals, incorrect payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted delivery, lost observation and restoration of the wrong generation. The customer operates an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Both retain notification and acknowledgment, financial and delivery states, response/recovery times, corrections and the receiving engineer’s reopening after restart. Monitoring gaps remain visible until observation resumes.

|Measure|Counting and acceptance|

|Completed purchase|One distinct approved intent, independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Deduplicate transactions per network; retain asset amounts and fees separately.|
|Prepaid purchase|Count the settled pass once, with at least one agreed operation and complete accepted output. Further calls and allowance units are usage. An unused pass retains unfinished fulfillment; a replacement needs its own settlement and first useful completion.|
|Complete customer task|Receive and accept every agreed page, file or application result. Retain started tasks, aggregate cost and unfinished coverage beside individual priced requests.|
|Independent and returning buyers|Count the accountable organization/person across its agents and wallets. Both merchants need independent use. Return use requires a distinct qualifying purchase on another UTC day.|
|Two facilitators|Complete the same useful service, schema, source population and output through each independent operator, preserving the actual terms and financial result.|
|Recovery and handover|Continue original requests and financial outcomes; reopen selected files/history, reconcile later operations and complete the maintainer’s support case.|

## 1. Customer problem and commercial model

An API or data-service operator needs to expose a useful resource to agent applications while retaining access rules, source meaning and commercial control. A buyer needs the complete result it approved and a way to resolve an interrupted paid request. The difficult join spans four records: approved request, settled transfer, delivered output and accepted fulfillment or accounting.

Current x402 reports show the practical need for that join. One October 2 report described payment-bearing requests rejected because a merchant required POST while the reference client retried GET; health and catalogue checks had appeared normal. The author subsequently corrected the server. An October 3 report described settlement without a discovery listing, with later indexing and facilitator diagnostics in the thread. These were Base deployments. They show how a healthy catalogue or settled payment can leave the customer's task unfinished. Our Stellar implementation retains the exact request and each original outcome so the unfinished step can be recovered. [Method report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3657) · [Discovery report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3677)

We serve recurring API/data-service operators, the developers using their results and agencies commissioned to integrate them. A fixed-fee implementation delivers one agreed operation and a handover the receiving engineer can maintain. Further care has its own scope. The commissioning payer, merchant controlling the resource and independent buyer may be different organizations. The workorder names each role, its source and host authority, payment responsibility and acceptance owner. The merchant retains its API or product receipts; TokenJunkieLabs invoices the implementation.

The selected customer task and the priced unit are recorded together. A complete report may require several paid pages. A handover may contain many files or transport chunks. The buyer retains per-request and aggregate spending controls while the operating record shows whether the whole task is complete. A later reporting period, changed source edition, fresh query or new order gives the same buyer a reason to use the service again.

## 2. Product architecture and control

Six connected components form the application: the merchant's private source/release workspace; its HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and configured facilitator; the buyer's private approval and spending state; complete result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Merchant and buyer services run on their operators' hosts. Approved operations are public; administration, provider credentials, signer references and operating state stay private.

| Stage | Implemented customer control |
| --- | --- |
| Review and publish | Review a source edition or named live query, its arguments and schema, public fields, output limits and complete payment alternatives. Save rights, route, network, asset, recipient, atomic amount and authorization lifetime. Changes or withdrawal become new reviewed states. |
| Connect the source | Preserve original types, missing/null values, pagination and snapshot/live meaning. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth aliases select access and the existing quota/cache state. Retain the edition behind each result. |
| Approve and purchase | Save the actual endpoint, method or tool, arguments, payment option and result scope. Match remote schema and challenge to that selection before signing. Keep the per-payment ceiling and the application's aggregate reservation/budget owner. |
| Settle and deliver | Use the configured native SDK/facilitator for verification and settlement. Save the server's response, full output, byte identity and durable merchant notification. Independently reconcile transaction network, asset, payer, payee and atomic amount. |
| Use and maintain | Receive every selected page or file into the customer's existing application, query, report or workbook. Preserve the parent acquisition and earlier source editions. Existing order and finance authorities control fulfillment, refunds and accounting. |
| Deploy and receive | Select the release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. Drain, restart, roll back and restore with the original configuration, history and complete customer files. |

The native x402 flow reuses the existing Exact Stellar scheme, token contracts and facilitator supported/verification/settlement interfaces. For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments remain distinct from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge; the full payment option must match the saved quote before the signed call is dispatched. The official MCP SDK transports the payment and settlement metadata.

Server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete useful output, receiver acknowledgment and order fulfillment remain separately visible. An uncertain signed reply retains its dispatch state for reconciliation. Reopening a consumed quote returns saved work. Recovery of a complete retained result uses that saved result. A new request or changed purchase gets its own review. Complete export and restore carry the configuration, history and referenced files; the receiving host supplies current authorized secret references.

Browser, CLI, MCP and installed Applications use these same saved workspaces. Native source registrations connect setup, operation and lifecycle while preserving each source adapter's data semantics. The existing request-collection, buyer-to-Operations and document-analysis extensions retain their own original recovery operations; their pending native receiving stages are reported separately from the completed examples below.

## Service recovery that reaches the buyer’s books

### The customer outcome

A buyer needs the useful service it purchased and a correct record of what happened when delivery failed. The merchant may recover the output, agree a partial return or identify a remaining correction. The buyer then needs the credit to reach the right expense item, reporting period and accountant handoff. Keeping those links saves staff from repeatedly matching support tickets, payment records, exported files and bookkeeping rows.

The Service-to-buyer operation carries that work through one saved customer case. The merchant selects its Service report and explicit monetary basis. Its configured accounting operator reviews the adjustment and the returned-transfer evidence. The buyer receives the complete capture, codes the original purchase and credit, resolves period issues and issues the period. The accountant’s reviewed return comes back to those original rows. A receiving engineer can reopen the continued project with its source, decisions and customer files.

### Architecture and operator control

The existing merchant workspace owns the Service terms, report, proposal, prepared intent and native outcome. The configured accounting workspace verifies the selected payment and adjustment and exports the original purchase, linked credit and complete adjustment statuses. Buyer Expenses owns source intake, exact native-unit allocations, issue dispositions and issued periods. The Accountant workspace owns its handoff and permitted returned fields.

Each step uses the configured owner’s existing workspace and request journal. Before dispatch, the operator reviews the exact input and original workspace selection. When a response is interrupted, recovery reuses the retained request and body; an already committed result is returned before applying a current-version check. Appending the outcome preserves other operators’ intervening case work. The complete export carries the applications, buyer state, issued period, accountant files and original requests together.

The monetary decision stays explicit: the Service report supplies the observed event and reviewed basis; the responsible operator authorizes the adjustment. The original purchase, adjustment status, returned-transfer proof and buyer coding remain separately inspectable throughout receiving.

## Customer value and delivery economics

Let F be the one-time implementation fee, V the customer’s stated value of an hour, H the measured active hours saved per equivalent completed task, N the number of useful repeat tasks, and C the period’s incremental provider, hosting, payment and support cost. The direct labor-value comparison is `N × H × V − F − C`; the effort reduction per task needed to recover the fee is `(F + C) / (N × V)`.

### Reopen the retained purchase

Use the maintained runtime installation with native Stellar packages, the MCP feature and operator support. Retain the selected source archive, complete lock and READY installation. In Applications choose **Grant purchase reviewer**, select that runtime and a private workbench directory, then use **Review → Save → Connect → Start → Open**. Leaving Packet and SHA-256 empty selects the bundled original purchase; an existing exported packet uses its exact digest. The installed command is:

~~~sh
starforge grant-demo workbench --dir /srv/starforge/state/grant-review --port 0
~~~

The full original guide covers private parent ownership, instance access, both retained quotes, complete results, closed Buyer export and receiving. This route reopens retained work; opening the page itself does not launch an application.
